# DRAFT: Medical device adverse incident report

> This is a draft for human review. It has not been submitted. A manufacturer would report
> through the MHRA MORE portal; healthcare professionals and users report through the Yellow Card scheme.

## 1. Device
- Name: ClinicDrift-monitored DR screening model
- Version: v1.0
- Intended use: screening retinal photographs for referable diabetic retinopathy

## 2. Where and when
- Clinic: IN-APT-01 (India)
- Period: week 1 (starting 2026-01-05)

## 3. What happened
ClinicDrift found that the scans from this clinic no longer resemble the scans used to validate the AI (drift score 0.99, where 0.5 indicates similarity to training data and 1 indicates a clear difference). 

As expert grades for the 50 scans from this week have not yet been received, the catch rate (sensitivity for referable disease) cannot be verified. The AI is referring more patients than usual, accounting for 80% of this week's scans compared with 68% of the training scans.

## 4. Potential patient impact
As the catch rate cannot be verified, no estimate has been made for possibly missed cases. No patient harm has been confirmed.

## 5. Likely cause
Changes to camera settings or hardware configuration have led to severely reduced image resolution, lower sharpness, poorer overall image quality, and altered brightness and contrast compared to the training data. (Category: camera or image quality; confidence 95%; source: gemini)

Evidence:
- Drift alarm with a high drift score of 0.99
- Mean brightness dropped from 0.373 in training to 0.294 in flagged scans (relative change -0.211)
- Mean contrast dropped from 0.0963 in training to 0.0647 in flagged scans (relative change -0.328)
- Mean sharpness dropped drastically from 0.000399 in training to 6.2e-05 in flagged scans (relative change -0.844)
- Mean quality dropped from 0.5 in training to 0.106 in flagged scans (relative change -0.789)
- Mean resolution decreased from 1020.0 pixels in training to 224.0 pixels in flagged scans (relative change -0.781)
- Referral rate increased from 0.685 in training to 0.8 in flagged scans

## 6. Action
ClinicDrift paused the AI at this clinic because the scans have drifted beyond the conditions for which the device was validated, meaning the catch rate cannot be verified. It is recommended that this clinic's scans are sent for human grading until the following checks are complete:

Checks:
- [ ] Inspect the physical camera lens and sensor for dirt, smudges, or obstruction
- [ ] Verify camera software resolution and export settings to ensure images are not being excessively downsampled
- [ ] Check illumination settings and calibration of the fundus camera
- [ ] Review technician training on proper focus, alignment, and capture protocols

## 7. Regulatory context
- Post-market surveillance (PMS): this alarm forms part of ongoing monitoring of the device in use.
- Predetermined change control plan (PCCP): any model change made in response should fall within an agreed PCCP.
- MHRA AI Airlock Phase 2 report: see recommendations 3 and 4.

## 8. MIT AI Risk Repository tags
- 7.3 AI system safety, failures & limitations > Lack of capability or robustness
- 1.3 Discrimination & toxicity > Unequal performance across groups
- 5.1 Human-computer interaction > Overreliance and unsafe use
